health_zone_table.basis: SitRep80 Tableau 2 (2026-08-02) transcribed and reconciled against the INSP PDF (15 pages, sha256 fae9db4cc474db768ed75063681811e09e5d9441e3e72aad2d47d3e2009692f1). Only the cumulative case and death columns are transcribed: the printed Letalite and 24-hour columns carry SitRep 79's values shifted down one row and are preserved as a source defect, not promoted. CFR is recomputed from the cumulative columns; per-zone 24-hour confirmations come from the section-1 narrative.

reconciliation.note: All 51 printed rows close exactly to 3802/1707 and every province total matches Tableau 1. Nord-Kivu declares a retrospective harmonization, so the cumulative step (+54 confirmed / +50 deaths) is NOT the day's incidence: 58 confirmations and 40 deaths were notified, and Nord-Kivu's reclassifications net -4 cases and +10 deaths against a simple report (400+18=418 / 262+9=271 restated to 414/285). Wanie-Rukula and Lubero are both officially integrated this cycle, taking the footprint to 51/140.

lab_indicators_24h.note: Usable source denominators yield 72 positives among 347 analyzed samples (20.7%) across Ituri, Nord-Kivu, Haut-Uele and Sud-Kivu. Tshopo reported no sampling for the day. Nord-Kivu's site split (47 Beni + 85 Butembo = 132) closes on the 132 received, which contradicts its own statement that 5 analyses remain pending; the site split is retained.

care_continuity: SitRep80 reports 707 patients in isolation (335 confirmed / 372 suspected) over 1050 reported beds, 67.3% national occupancy; Nord-Kivu is the acute pressure point at 186/141 = 131.9%.
Nord-Kivu has not reported bed capacity for seven cycles, so its occupancy rests on a carried denominator; the source's own challenge table cites six cycles and 128.4%, one cycle stale.

Haut-Uele patient movement still does not close: 33 prior patients plus 16 admissions minus 4 exits implies 45, while 31 are reported at day end, and its care tables are identical to the previous day.
Six Ituri CTE exceed confirmed-case saturation (Nizi 278%, ISTM 123%, CME 104%, Lita and Fataki 100%) and two exceed it for suspects (Fataki 200%, Aru 140%); 63 patients are severe or critical.
Sud-Kivu enters the care table for the first time with 20 suspects isolated at Lwiro, the Bukavu university clinics and Katana, but reports no bed capacity.
highlights: The official footprint expands to 51 of 140 health zones across five provinces: Lubero (Nord-Kivu) records its first confirmed case, a death, and Wanie-Rukula (Tshopo, confirmed 29 July) is integrated after harmonization.
The DRC headline is 3802 confirmed / 1707 deaths; all 51 printed rows close exactly to those totals and every province total matches Tableau 1.
Nord-Kivu declares a retrospective harmonization: the cumulative step of +54 confirmed and +50 deaths is a restatement, while 58 confirmations and 40 deaths were notified in 24 hours.
Nord-Kivu crosses 400 cumulative cases with a 68.8% fatality rate against Ituri's 41.7%; 48% of its day suspects are community deaths, indicating very late detection.
National contact follow-up falls to 79.2% (14466/18276) from 80.1%, with Mangala at 43.7%, Fataki at 51.8% and Bunia at 61.8% holding it down.
Alert investigation is 92.0% nationally but covers only three provinces; Nord-Kivu more than doubled its alert flow to 731 in a day while holding 99.6% investigation.
Tableau 2's fatality and 24-hour columns reprint SitRep 79's values shifted down one row, so only its cumulative columns are usable this cycle.

alerts_total.data_gap_note: SitRep80 Tableau 3 closes at 1265 alerts, 1164 investigated and 275 validated suspects across three reporting provinces. Haut-Uele and Tshopo transmitted no alert slide and are ND, so national totals cover Ituri, Nord-Kivu and Sud-Kivu only. Ituri's own total (531) exceeds its carry-over plus new alerts (15+507=522) by 9; the source recalculates its investigation rate on 531 and that basis is kept.

challenges.finding: Post-mortem sampling reluctance, community resistance and insecurity targeting burial teams (an attack at the Muchanga bridge, activities paralysed at Nyankunde) delay confirmation and under-estimate cases.
challenges.response: Intensify RCCE, involve religious and community leaders, secure teams and increase burial-team capacity.

challenges.finding: Provider non-payment and strikes in Bunia and Rwampara interrupt response activities including safe and dignified burials; a resumption is announced after the Ituri military governor's intervention.
challenges.response: Regularise provider payment and secure dedicated financing.

challenges.finding: CTE/CT capacity is insufficient: Nord-Kivu is over capacity and five Ituri structures are at or above confirmed-case capacity, including Nizi at 278%.
challenges.response: Accelerate CTE construction and expansion, deploy temporary structures and report bed capacity systematically.

challenges.finding: Contact follow-up remains below target at 79.2% nationally, with Haut-Uele carried unchanged, Tshopo not reporting, and Damas, Logo and Kambala without usable data.
challenges.response: Train, deploy and motivate community relays; reinforce supervision.

challenges.finding: Insufficient ambulances and pre-positioning at control points delay transfer and isolation.
challenges.response: Pre-position ambulances including at PoE/PoC and deploy treatment capacity by health zone.

challenges.finding: Insufficient essential medicines and medical inputs weaken holistic case management.
challenges.response: Urgently procure and distribute essential medicines.

challenges.finding: Insufficient IPC inputs and only 181 of 1170 triage units functional raise nosocomial risk; the source cites 141 Ituri frontline infections with 41 deaths against its own Tableau 8 total of 140 with 43 deaths.
challenges.response: Urgently procure IPC supplies and reinforce IPC training.

challenges.finding: Extension to Haut-Uele and Tshopo alongside high mobility raises urban, riverine and cross-border spread risk.
challenges.response: Activate the 23 priority Haut-Uele PoE/PoC and reinforce cross-border coordination.

challenges.finding: Proximity laboratories are still being installed at Rwampara, Fataki, Bambu-mine, Boga and Mambasa, prolonging confirmation delays.
challenges.response: Accelerate deployment of decentralised diagnostic capacity.

challenges.finding: Insufficient financial resources limit implementation across response pillars.
challenges.response: Mobilise resources urgently and advocate with partners.

challenges.finding: Insecurity and limited access linked to CODECO and ADF restrict operations.
challenges.response: Reinforce security coordination and humanitarian access.

challenges.finding: Continuity of essential health services is compromised, raising indirect non-Ebola mortality.
challenges.response: Implement free care effectively and reinforce continuity of essential health services.

contacts_total.data_gap_note: Tableau 4 arithmetically closes at 14466/18276 = 79.2%. Tshopo reported nothing this cycle and Haut-Uele's 375/562 is byte-identical to SitRep 79, so it is carried, not fresh telemetry.

patient_movement_total.data_gap_note: SitRep80 Tableau 6 reports 707 end-of-day patients over 1050 reported beds (Sud-Kivu capacity is ND). Provincial flows imply 722 (711 + 147 - 136), leaving a 15-patient gap: 14 in Haut-Uele, whose movement the source itself flags as unclosed (45 expected against 31 reported), and 1 in Nord-Kivu. Ituri and Sud-Kivu close exactly.

priorities.priority: Relieve Nord-Kivu's 131.9% occupancy and restore the bed-capacity reporting it has not filed for seven cycles.
Restore alert reporting in Haut-Uele and Tshopo, which transmitted no slide at all this cycle.
Raise national follow-up from 79.2% toward 95%, starting with Mangala at 43.7% and the 2062 unseen Ituri contacts.
Restore triage and IPC inputs: only 181/1170 triage units are functional while frontline infections continue.
Close Nord-Kivu's late-detection gap: 48% of its day suspects are community deaths and its CFR is 68.8%.
Repair Tableau 2, whose fatality and 24-hour columns reprint SitRep 79 values shifted by one row.

preserved_conflicts: SitRep80 national headline is DRC-only (3802 confirmed / 1707 deaths); the country-scope snapshot adds Uganda 20/2/11 separately -> 3822 confirmed / 1709 deaths / 738 recovered.

TABLEAU 2 COLUMN DEFECT: the printed Letalite column and the whole 24-hour block (Nouv. cas, community deaths, intra-CTE deaths, total deaths) are SitRep 79's values shifted down one row. Adja's 41,5% is SitRep 79's Ituri province CFR and Adja's 49/13/10/23 is SitRep 79's Ituri province day block; the same shift holds for Beni (Nord-Kivu's SR79 day block) and Isiro (Haut-Uele's). Only the cumulative case and death columns are promoted; CFR is recomputed and 24-hour zone detail is taken from the narrative.

NORD-KIVU HARMONIZATION: a simple report gives 418 cases / 271 deaths (400+18 / 262+9) but the province publishes 414/285 after retrospective reclassification, principally Katwa (+6 cases, +14 deaths) and Butembo (-1 case, +2 deaths). The cumulative delta is therefore -4 cases and +10 deaths against notified movement and is not 24-hour incidence.

DAY-DEATH COUNT CONFLICT: the cover reports +40 deaths for the day (Ituri 23, Nord-Kivu 14, Haut-Uele 3) plus 10 by harmonization, while the narrative bullet says 37 confirmed deaths. The 37 equals Ituri 23 + Nord-Kivu 14 and omits Haut-Uele's 3; the cover's 40 reconciles with the +50 cumulative step and is retained.

HAUT-UELE ATTRIBUTION CONFLICT: the narrative attributes the province's single new confirmation to an Isiro swab, but the cumulative table leaves Isiro at 19 and raises Boma Mangbetu from 12 to 13. The table is promoted; both readings are preserved.

ITURI ALERT ARITHMETIC: the provincial table totals 531 alerts while its carry-over (15) plus new alerts (507) give 522. The source attributes the 9-alert gap to three zonal lines that do not close internally (Bambu, Mangala, Mongbwalu) and recalculates investigation at 81,5% against 84% announced; the recalculated basis is kept.

PATIENT FLOW CONFLICT: 711 prior patients plus 147 admissions minus 136 exits implies 722, but 707 are reported at day end. Haut-Uele accounts for 14 of the 15-patient gap and Nord-Kivu for 1; Ituri and Sud-Kivu close exactly.

OCCUPANCY VINTAGE CONFLICT: Tableau 6 reports Nord-Kivu at 131,9% while challenge 3 cites 128,4% (the SitRep 79 value) and says capacity has been unreported for six cycles against the narrative's seven. The current table value is promoted.

FRONTLINE-WORKER CONFLICT: Tableau 8 totals 140 Ituri frontline cases with 43 deaths while challenge 7 cites 141 with 41 deaths; the outcome breakdown totals only 139 and its recovered column sums to 73 against a printed 71. The source itself flags that the cumulative fell from 142 in SitRep 79, breaching non-regression.
SUD-KIVU INTERVAL CONFLICT: the source states 53 days without a confirmed case since 10 June and immediately notes the real interval is 52 days; both are preserved.
CURRENTNESS LIMIT: Haut-Uele contact figures are byte-identical to SitRep 79 and Tshopo transmitted no alert or contact slide, so those table values are carried, not fresh telemetry.

review_notes: SitRep #080 reports 2026-08-02 and was published 2026-08-03 through INSP post 25249/media 25250.
All 15 pages were rendered and reviewed individually; they are ordered, upright, nonblank and readable.
Fifty-one printed zone rows close exactly to 3802 confirmed / 1707 deaths and every province total matches Tableau 1.
Tableau 2's fatality and 24-hour columns reprint the previous SitRep's values shifted down one row; only the cumulative columns are promoted and the defect is preserved as a conflict.
Official coverage expands to 51/140: Lubero enters with its first confirmed case and Wanie-Rukula is integrated after Tshopo harmonization.
Nord-Kivu's declared harmonization makes the cumulative step a restatement; notified 24-hour movement is 58 confirmations and 40 deaths.
